title: Secretary Rubio’s Call with Bahraini Foreign Minister Al Zayani
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Readout


			
			


			
			
November 16, 2026
Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke today with Bahraini Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani. The Secretary condemned Iran’s attacks on Bahrain and reaffirmed the commitment of the United States to the security of Bahrain and all our Gulf partners.  The Secretary and the Foreign Minister also reaffirmed the long-standing U.S.-Bahrain strategic partnership, anchored by Bahrain’s designation as a Major Non-NATO Ally and the Comprehensive Security Integration and Prosperity Agreement (C-SIPA).

title: Reward Offers Totaling Up to $20 Million for Information Leading to Arrests and/or Convictions of Guatemalan Narcoterrorists
summary_raw:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
November 16, 2026
Today, the Department of State’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs is announcing reward offers under the Narcotics Rewards Program (NRP) of up to $10 million each for information leading to the arrests and/or convictions, in any country, of Guatemalan narcoterrorists Axel Bladimir Montejo Saenz, a.k.a. “Mosh,” and Walfre Donaldo Calderón-Calderón, a.k.a. “El Teniente Jr.”
Montejo Saenz and Calderón-Calderón are wanted for drug trafficking, extortion, weapons trafficking, human trafficking, and murder across the Guatemala-Mexico border.  They operate in association with the Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación (CJNG), a Foreign Terrorist Organization designated by the Trump Administration last year. 
On November 1, 2018, Montejo Saenz was charged in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California with international cocaine distribution conspiracy.  On May 31, 2019, Calderón-Calderón was also charged in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California with international cocaine distribution conspiracy.
Today’s reward offers are authorized by the Assistant Secretary for International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs under the NRP, which supports law enforcement efforts to disrupt transnational drug trafficking globally and bring fugitives to justice.  If you have information, please contact Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) at +1-619-643-2325 (WhatsApp/Telegram/Signal).  f you are located outside of the United States, you may also contact the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate.  If you are in the United States, you may also contact the local HSI office in your city.
ALL IDENTITIES ARE KEPT STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL.  Government officials and employees are not eligible for rewards based on information provided in the course of official duty.

title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Federated States of Micronesia President Simina
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Readout


			
			


			
			
November 16, 2026
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met today with Federated States of Micronesia (FSM) President Wesley Simina to continue discussions on the bilateral relationship, which is based on a Compact of Free Association.  The Deputy Secretary reaffirmed that the Compact remains the gold standard for U.S. partnership in the Pacific, and the two leaders pledged to continue cooperating under its framework by, among other things, convening foreign affairs consultations, following through on Typhoon Sinlaku disaster relief, and expanding Veteran Affairs healthcare to FSM veterans of the U.S. armed forces.  The Deputy Secretary also discussed avenues to deepen security and economic cooperation, including previewing the second Pacific Investment Summit, planned for February 2027 at the East-West Center in Honolulu.  Deputy Secretary Landau also congratulated President Simina on the 40th anniversary of FSM’s independence and the opening of FSM’s new embassy in Washington, DC.

title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Travel to Tajikistan, Türkiye, and Turkmenistan
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 16, 2026
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau will travel to Dushanbe, Tajikistan; Istanbul, Türkiye; and Ashgabat, Turkmenistan from November 16-24.
In Dushanbe, Deputy Secretary Landau will meet with senior Tajik government officials and private sector leaders to further deepen U.S.-Tajikistan cooperation on regional connectivity, economic growth, and Super Intelligence technology and innovation. He will reaffirm the strong security partnership that is stopping terrorism and transnational crime, highlight a health memorandum of understanding under the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy, advance U.S. commercial interests, support cultural heritage preservation, and highlight how U.S. investment creates opportunities for both the United States and Tajikistan.
The Deputy Secretary will then travel to Istanbul to meet with senior Turkish government officials and business leaders to discuss areas of cooperation in the U.S.-Türkiye bilateral relationship. He will advance commercial ties and promote U.S. companies, protecting U.S. jobs and ensuring lasting American prosperity. Deputy Secretary Landau will also promote U.S. energy and supply chain security.
In Ashgabat, Deputy Secretary Landau will meet with Turkmen government leaders and executives from the Turkmen and U.S. business communities. He will emphasize that the United States is committed to expanding cooperation with Turkmenistan on energy export diversification along the Trans-Caspian corridor and the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity. The Deputy Secretary will underscore the importance of strengthening economic ties and promoting shared prosperity through increased trade, investment, and regional connectivity.

title: United States Welcomes Election of Jennifer Warren to the International Telecommunication Union Radio Regulations Board
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 16, 2026

The United States welcomes the election of Jennifer Warren to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Radio Regulations Board (RRB).
Ms. Warren brings more than 30 years of regulatory experience spanning government, the private sector, academia, and industry associations, along with longstanding engagement at the ITU.  Her proven record of public service and deep understanding of the challenges facing the RRB make her well-qualified to serve on the Board.  She brings a strong commitment to independence, accountability, and sound decision-making.
The United States welcomes the experience and leadership Ms. Warren will bring to the RRB as it works to strengthen confidence in its decisions and deliver meaningful results for ITU Member States.
